name: X (Twitter)
description: Anonymous X (Twitter) collection over the guest-token path used by the Fritter/Squawker client family — no API key, no login. Two plugins: X Profile (identify accounts, two requests per node) and X Posts (collect their timelines). Both run the whole selection under one guest session, minted once. Desktop only: X sends no CORS headers, so the desktop shell must allowlist api.twitter.com and twitter.com. X Profile is reliable; X Posts returns nothing for some accounts, for reasons X does not document.

plugins.name: X Profile
plugins.description: Fetches each selected X (Twitter) account's public profile — display name, bio, location, website, follower/following/post counts, verification, join date, avatar — through the anonymous guest-token path, and folds it into the Social Account node. Two requests per node: use this to identify or verify accounts before deciding whether a timeline is worth collecting. One guest session serves the whole selection. No API key, no login. Desktop only: X answers no CORS preflight, so the shell must waive its origins first — the Run plugins dialog offers that as one click.

network.purpose: Guest-token activation (the anonymous session every read runs under).
X internal GraphQL: UserByScreenName (profile) and UserTweets (timeline).

plugins.name: X Posts
plugins.description: Collects each selected X (Twitter) account's recent posts through the anonymous guest-token path: one Post node per tweet with its text, timestamp, engagement counts and permalink, plus Hashtag and Media nodes and 'posted by' / 'uses hashtag' / 'contains media' / 'reposted' / 'replies to' edges. Skips the profile lookup entirely when a node already carries a user_id. One guest session serves the whole selection. No API key, no login. Desktop only. UNRELIABLE BY ACCOUNT: X answers this unofficial path inconsistently and returns an empty timeline for some accounts - smaller ones most often, roughly under a thousand followers, but that is a tendency and not a threshold, and accounts well above it have gone both ways. The profile still reads fine, and the posts are still visible in a browser; there is no setting that changes it.

network.purpose: Guest-token activation (the anonymous session every read runs under).
X internal GraphQL: UserByScreenName (profile) and UserTweets (timeline).

count.title: Posts
count.description: How many recent posts to collect (1-100). X ignores this per request, so the plugin pages until it has that many.
